content.user_title: Create Clear Documents Through Guided Co-Authoring
content.value_statement: Complex documents often stall because context, structure, and reader needs remain unclear. This skill guides collaborative drafting, targeted revision, and reader testing through a structured workflow.
actual_capabilities: Gathers document goals, audience details, constraints, templates, and supporting context through focused questions.
Proposes appropriate section structures for specifications, proposals, decision documents, and other substantial writing tasks.
Guides each section through clarification, brainstorming, curation, gap checks, drafting, and iterative refinement.
Creates Markdown scaffolds and applies targeted edits when compatible file or artifact tools are available.
Tests document clarity with subagents or provides a manual workflow using a fresh Claude conversation.
limitations: Requires the user to provide or authorize access to source context and shared documents.
Cannot validate factual claims, links, or technical details without reliable source material.
Reader testing depends on subagent access or manual execution by the user.
Complex documents may require several iterations and still need accountable human review.

use_cases.title: Draft an Engineering RFC
use_cases.description: Capture architecture, constraints, alternatives, trade-offs, and open questions in a document that reviewers can understand.

use_cases.title: Build a Product Proposal
use_cases.description: Turn stakeholder context and product goals into a structured proposal or requirements document.

use_cases.title: Improve Internal Guidance
use_cases.description: Refine procedures, handbooks, and operating documents, then test whether fresh readers can use them correctly.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through the three-stage workflow to create a [document type] for [audience]. Begin by asking the initial context questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a document with limited structure.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me refine this outline for [audience] and [goal]. Identify missing sections, ask clarifying questions, then draft one section at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developing an early outline into a complete document.

prompt_templates.title: Co-Author a Technical Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Co-author a decision document about [decision]. Compare [options], capture constraints and trade-offs, and preserve my reasoning through targeted section edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Documenting a complex technical or organizational decision.

prompt_templates.title: Run Independent Reader Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this completed [document type] as a fresh reader. Predict likely questions, identify ambiguity and assumptions, then propose precise revisions for every gap.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validating an advanced draft before publication.

output_examples.input: I need an RFC for replacing our deployment pipeline.
output: Audience: Who approves the change, and who operates the current pipeline?
Impact: What outcome should readers support after reviewing the RFC?
Constraints: Which reliability, migration, budget, and timeline limits must the proposal address?

output_examples.input: Help organize my proposal notes into sections.
Test whether a new reader can understand this decision document.
output_examples.output: The reader can identify the selected option, but the approval criteria and migration owner remain unclear. Add both details before final review.

best_practices: Provide the audience, purpose, decision constraints, and reliable source material before drafting.
Review one section at a time and explain why requested changes improve the document.
Validate facts independently and complete reader testing before publishing the final document.
anti_patterns: Starting a complete draft before sharing the audience, goals, constraints, or available template.
Providing sensitive internal information without confirming access permissions and data-handling requirements.
Treating reader testing as a substitute for factual, legal, security, or technical review.

faq.question: What documents can this skill help create?
faq.answer: It supports proposals, technical specifications, decision documents, RFCs, requirements documents, and other structured writing.

faq.question: Does the workflow require a template?
faq.answer: No. It can follow an existing template or propose a suitable section structure.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing document?
faq.answer: Yes, when the document is provided directly or through an authorized integration.

faq.question: How does reader testing work?
faq.answer: A fresh agent answers likely reader questions and checks ambiguity, assumptions, and contradictions.

faq.question: What happens when subagents are unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill provides steps for testing the document manually in a fresh Claude conversation.

faq.question: Does it verify every fact in the document?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify facts, links, technical details, and accountable decisions before publication.
